samples.summary: New `readOnly` presence gate in `YorkieDocStore` has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds a `readOnly` constructor arg to `YorkieDocStore` and two early returns (`updateCursorPos`/`publishResolvedLocalCursor` at ~line 1263 and ~3196) that suppress presence writes while still claiming caret anchoring keeps working. Every call of `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/*` (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, editor-undo-selection.test.ts, merge-repro.test.ts, helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts) passes one argument only; grepping `readOnly` across packages/frontend/tests returns no docs-store file. The sibling spreadsheet gate got a whole dedicated file (tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts), so the asymmetry is visible: if this gate regresses (either direction) a share-link viewer either wedges their own sync on the first click or loses caret anchoring, with nothing failing.

samples.summary: `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` read-only early-return is untested, and so is `sheet-view`'s `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` gate
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }` to `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` and calls it the engine-level backstop ('so neither this call site nor a future one can leak it'). `grep recalculateCrossSheetFormulas packages/sheets` shows tests only for `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (test/sheet/cross-sheet-*.test.ts), none constructing a read-only `Spreadsheet`; the only read-only view test, test/view/worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts, covers `finishEditing` only. Frontend-side, `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)` in sheet-view.tsx have no test either (no sheet-view test file). A regression re-enables a viewer's recalc write, which the webhook refuses and which wedges that viewer's sync — the exact failure this change exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Slides read-only gates at the call sites (presence `broadcast`, `ensureSlidesRoot(readOnly)`) are untested; only the store helper is covered

Grep for `updatePresence|onSelectionChange` under packages/frontend/tests returns only slides toolbar/state tests, none of which mount SlidesView read-only.

samples.summary: `onActivePageChange`'s new read-only early return is untested

The other half of the change — `if (readOnly || !doc || …) return` in `onActivePageChange` — has no coverage: grepping `activePage|onActivePageChange|readOnly` in tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx yields only `readOnly={false}` on a mount, no assertion about the presence publish being suppressed.

samples.summary: Board selection-presence read-only gate has no test

samples.summary: New `readOnly` prop on CommentPopover (and its new message branch) has no test
samples.evidence: `isReadOnly = readOnly || currentUser === null` and the new 'You have view-only access to this document.' branch are untested: grep for `CommentPopover` across packages/frontend matches only source files (yorkie-store.ts, sheet-view.tsx, CommentPopover.tsx, docs-view.tsx, DocsCommentPopover.tsx) — no test file references it. samples.summary: Missing-secret branches of the service-token helpers are untested, as is `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` and the scripts' no-fallback rule
samples.evidence: `grep signYorkieServiceToken|yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` in packages/backend shows the only test references are in auth/auth.service.spec.ts, which covers signing/verification and the scoped `yorkieServiceTokenInjector` happy path. Nothing asserts (a) `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(undefined)` returns `undefined`, (b) `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()` warns and returns undefined with no `JWT_SECRET`, (c) `YorkieService` warns and omits the injector when `JWT_SECRET` is unset (yorkie.service.spec.ts's mock config always supplies it), or (d) `sideTokenInjector` in scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts never falls back between SOURCE/TARGET secrets — the rule the file's own doc comment calls the security-critical one. There is no spec file for yorkie-service-token.ts or yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts.

samples.summary: Divider hit-area/touch-action and the new split-ratio `track` math are untested
samples.evidence: The diff changes the divider from 7px to a 25px hit area, adds `touchAction: 'none'`, and changes the drag ratio denominator from `rect.width` to `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`. packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts adds only read-only tests; no test drags the divider or asserts the resulting pane flex-basis, so a wrong denominator (visible pointer lag) or a lost `touch-action` (split unresizable on touch) ships silently.

samples.summary: 'keeps refusing a viewer PushPull write after a permitted attach' does not exercise anything post-attach
samples.evidence: The test builds a fresh controller and issues a single PushPull with verb `rw`, asserting 403 — byte-for-byte the same path already asserted by 'lets a share viewer read but not write' (line 241). No attach is performed and the controller holds no per-client state, so the name's 'after a permitted attach' is not what is tested; it reads as coverage of attach/PushPull sequencing that does not exist.

samples.summary: Non-persistence is asserted only for viewMode, not for keymap or showAuthors
samples.evidence: The file's docstring claims 'nothing written back to the visitor's stored preferences', but only the view-mode change asserts localStorage is unchanged. `setKeymap`/`setShowAuthors` are passed straight to the toolbar with no test that changing them leaves `notes-settings` storage untouched, so a future `writeKeymap` slipping into this layout would pass.

verdict.reason: The readOnly presence gate in YorkieDocStore is genuinely untested. The code exists as claimed (field/ctor at yorkie-doc-store.ts:604-608, early returns at :1263 and :3199, sole flag-passing caller docs-view.tsx:364). Searching wider than the reviewer's paths: every `new YorkieDocStore(` in tests/helpers repo-wide passes a single argument (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36, editor-undo-selection.test.ts:102, merge-repro.test.ts:55, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:90, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111/137). A repo-wide grep of `readOnly` limited to test/spec files yields only component-level docs gates (docs-find-bar-read-only, docs-context-menu, docs-table-context-menu), the separate engine seam packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts (readOnlyDocStore, which the store's own comment says does not cover presence), and the sibling spreadsheet file. The indirect route is closed too: no test mounts DocsView anywhere (only prose mentions in two menu tests), there is no e2e suite in the repo, and yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts never mentions readOnly/viewer. So no test can observe either failure direction: a viewer publishing presence (rw PushPull the auth webhook refuses, wedging that viewer's own sync), or the gate moved above the anchor bookkeeping at :3191-3194, silently losing viewer caret anchoring. Missing coverage over a changed user-visible path is major in this lens.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the read-only early return exists at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:971-979 and the frontend gates at sheet-view.tsx:1308 and :1322, but no test exercises either. Repo-wide greps show `new Spreadsheet(` appears only at spreadsheet.ts:49 (no test ever constructs the view class, read-only or not); the `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` tests in packages/sheets/test/sheet/cross-sheet-{cycle,calculation}.test.ts drive the Sheet model, and yorkie-cross-sheet.integration.ts contains no readOnly at all. There is no sheet-view test file in packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet (13 files, none targets it), and remote-change-utils.test.ts tests needsRecalc(ops) in isolation without the `readOnly ? false : …` gate. The closest candidate counterexample, yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts, only covers presence, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder and comment writes, matching the store's only readOnly gates (yorkie-store.ts:109, 651, 689, 1311); cell/formula-cache writes are ungated in the store, so that suite cannot fail if the Spreadsheet gate regresses. A regression therefore ships silently and re-enables a viewer write the auth webhook refuses, wedging that viewer's sync — a missing test over a guard on a user-visible path, major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: New `readOnly` gate in YorkieStore (presence seed, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff adds three write suppressions in `YorkieStore`: the constructor's `p.set({activeTabId})` seed, `updateSelection()` and `ensureAxisOrder()`. `sheet-view.tsx` now passes `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, readOnly)`. Nothing tests any of them: `rg readOnly packages/frontend/tests` returns only docs/pdf/shared-header hits, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60` constructs `new YorkieStore(doc as never, tabId)` with no third argument, so every `ensureAxisOrder` case (lines 73–117) exercises only the writable path. The parameter defaults to `false`, so a regression that drops the flag (e.g. `sheet-view` forgetting to pass it, or the guard being placed after the `doc.update`) leaves the whole existing suite green while a share-link viewer either writes `rowOrder`/`colOrder` into the CRDT root or has their sync denied on the first arrow key. The existing axis-order test file already has a doc harness, so a `readOnly` variant is cheap.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file covering exactly the three claimed-untested gates exists and runs: packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts. It constructs the real YorkieStore with the third `readOnly` argument (line 68) over a real @yorkie-js/sdk Document seeded from initialSpreadsheetDocument() (lines 41-51), instrumenting doc.update only to count invocations (lines 53-58) — the store's real logic executes, so this is not over-mocking. Each gate is asserted in BOTH directions, so the tests cannot pass if the flag were dropped or the guard placed after doc.update: constructor presence seed writable=1 vs read-only=0 (lines 89-95, gating yorkie-store.ts:109-113); updateSelection writable=1 vs read-only=0 across two cursor moves (lines 97-114, gating yorkie-store.ts:651); ensureAxisOrder writable grows rowOrder/colOrder to 6/3 while read-only yields 0 updates and unchanged orders (lines 116-134, gating yorkie-store.ts:689). Read paths and the assertWritable comment mutators are also covered (lines 136-141, 164-196). The file is executed by the suite per packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:373-377 (test.include = tests/**/*.test.ts). The reviewer's reported empty searches do not reproduce: `rg readOnly packages/frontend/tests` returns this file, and `new YorkieStore` matches its lines 68 and 190. The reviewer's point that yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60 uses only two arguments is true but immaterial — the readOnly coverage lives in the separate file above.
